examples.en: I took an oral exam when I entered graduate school.
An oral exam makes me more nervous than a written one.
In the Korean oral exam, you have to introduce yourself.
The oral exam results will be announced next week.
The teacher evaluates pronunciation through an oral exam.

examples.ko: 내일 구술시험이 있어서 밤새 말하기를 연습했어요.
examples.en: I have an oral exam tomorrow, so I practiced speaking all night.

explain: 종이에 쓰는 '필기시험'과 반대로 말로 답하는 시험이에요. 사람을 뽑는 자리의 '면접'과 달리, 지식이나 실력을 말로 확인하는 시험을 가리켜요. '구술시험을 보다/치르다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of a '필기시험' (written test) because you answer by speaking. Unlike a '면접' (interview) for selecting people, it refers to an exam that checks knowledge or skill by speech. People say '구술시험을 보다' or '구술시험을 치르다'.

examples.en: I am jobless now, so I am looking for work.
I wrote 'unemployed' in the occupation box on the form.
I get anxious when the jobless period gets long.
I was jobless but got a job last month.

examples.ko: 무직인 사람도 지원금을 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even people without jobs can apply for the support money.
My jobless older brother helps with the housework.

explain: 서류의 직업 칸이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때는 '백수'라고 해요. 학생이나 주부는 보통 '무직' 대신 '학생', '주부'라고 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word seen in the occupation box on forms and in the news. Friends casually say '백수'. Students and homemakers usually write '학생' or '주부' instead of '무직'.

examples.en: I study law at university.

examples.ko: 법학 수업은 읽을 자료가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: Law classes have a lot of reading material.
My older sister plans to go to law school.
Many people who majored in law applied.
That professor is famous in the field of law.
I got interested in law, so I bought a book.

explain: 법을 연구하는 학문이라서 '법학과', '법학 박사', '법학을 전공하다'처럼 학문과 학교 이야기에서 써요. 법 자체는 '법', 법률 일을 하는 사람은 '변호사', '판사'라고 해요. '법학'은 법을 공부하고 연구하는 분야를, '법률'은 나라가 정한 규칙을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is the academic study of law, used in phrases like 법학과, 법학 박사 and 법학을 전공하다. The law itself is 법, and legal professionals are 변호사 or 판사. 법학 is the field of studying and researching law, while 법률 refers to the rules a country sets.

examples.en: I have no experience at all in this field.
You can say the risk of an accident is practically zero.
That team had never won a championship.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 큰 병원이 전무한 상태예요.
examples.en: This neighborhood has no large hospital at all.
How can you take the test when you have not prepared at all?
The chance is not zero, but it is very low.

explain: '없다'를 격식 있고 단호하게 말하는 표현이에요. 뉴스와 글에서 '경험이 전무하다', '사례가 전무하다'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '하나도 없어요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: A formal, emphatic way of saying '없다' (there is none). It appears in news and writing, as in '경험이 전무하다' (no experience at all). In everyday speech '하나도 없어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I changed careers from office worker to cook.

examples.ko: 교사에서 작가로 전직하는 사람이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people are switching from teaching to writing.
After I changed careers, my salary dropped a little.

examples.ko: 다른 업계로 전직할 기회를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a chance to move to another industry.
To change careers, you need a new certificate.
My friend changed careers and now works as a designer.

explain: 다른 지역이나 지점으로 옮기는 건 '전근', 회사를 옮기는 건 '이직', 직업의 종류를 바꾸는 건 '전직'이에요. 일상에서는 '직업을 바꾸다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Moving to another region or branch is '전근', changing companies is '이직', and changing the type of work you do is '전직'. In daily speech people also say '직업을 바꾸다' (change jobs).
